what: highlight "nearly half of the index's total market cap"
said: Right now, just twenty companies make up nearly half of the entire S and P five hundred.

what: highlight "it has posted annual increases 70% of the time"
said: And the stock market usually goes up. Over its history, the S and P five hundred has risen in about seven out of every ten years.

what: highlight "adds Nvidia and Tesla to the Big Five"
said: People call them the Magnificent Seven. Microsoft, Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Nvidia and Tesla.

what: highlight "accounted for approximately two-thirds of the S&P 500's gains"
said: In twenty twenty-three, those seven companies were responsible for about two thirds of the S and P five hundred's gains. Seven out of five hundred.

what: highlight "107% return on investment"
said: That same year, as a group, they more than doubled. A hundred and seven percent in one year, mostly on hopes about artificial intelligence.

what: highlight "accounted for 31% of the S&P 500"
said: Think about what that means for a regular saver. If Maya's fund puts one hundred dollars into the index, roughly thirty-one of those dollars go to just seven companies.

what: highlight "Employers are allowed to automatically enroll their employees in 401(k) plans"
said: This is called automatic enrollment. Your employer puts you into the retirement plan, and you have to opt out if you do not want it.

what: highlight "The Pension Protection Act of 2006 made automatic enrollment a safer option for employers"
said: Before two thousand six, many companies were nervous about doing this. Then a law changed the rules.

what: highlight "Bogle started the First Index Investment Trust on December 31, 1975"
said: The first one for regular people started on the last day of nineteen seventy-five. Its founder was John Bogle.

what: highlight "it was heavily derided by competitors"
said: Wall Street laughed at him. Competitors mocked the idea of just buying everything and doing nothing.

what: highlight "which it did in 2000"
said: Bogle predicted his boring fund would one day become bigger than the most famous stock-picking fund in America. It did, in the year two thousand.

what: highlight "79% of fund managers underperformed the S&P in 2021"
said: But doing nothing kept winning. In twenty twenty-one, seventy-nine percent of professional fund managers did worse than the S and P five hundred.

what: highlight "is the reacquisition by a company of its own shares"
said: The second engine is companies buying their own stock. This is called a share buyback.

what: highlight "there was a sharp rise in the volume of share repurchases in the United States"
said: In the past, companies mostly shared profits by paying cash to their owners. Today, many of them use buybacks instead.

what: highlight "representing almost 95% of all repurchases"
said: Most of it happens quietly, on the open market, just like any other buyer. Almost ninety-five percent of buybacks work this way.

what: highlight "HP spent $67 billion on stock buybacks"
said: Buybacks are not always smart, though. Between nineteen ninety-nine and twenty eleven, the computer company HP spent sixty-seven billion dollars buying back its own stock.

what: highlight "the Federal Reserve began lowering rates in September 2024"
said: After holding its key rate above five percent for over a year, the Federal Reserve started cutting in September twenty twenty-four.

what: highlight "The last cycle of easing monetary policy"
said: By December twenty twenty-five, the rate had come down to a range of about three and a half percent.

what: highlight "televised speech on December 5, 1996"
said: On December fifth, nineteen ninety-six, the head of the Federal Reserve gave a speech on live TV.

what: highlight "closing off 3%"
said: Markets in Tokyo dropped three percent within hours. People thought the top was in.

what: highlight "rose by 600%"
said: The tech-heavy Nasdaq, an index full of new internet companies, rose about six hundred percent between nineteen ninety-five and its peak.

what: highlight "successfully shorted many dot-com stocks at the peak of the bubble"
said: A few people saw the danger. The famous investor John Templeton bet against internet stocks at the very top and called it a time of temporary insanity.

what: highlight "the years clustered around 1929, 1999 and 2007"
said: The economist Robert Shiller found only three earlier periods when it was this high. The years around nineteen twenty-nine, nineteen ninety-nine, and two thousand seven.

what: highlight "reached an all-time high during the 2000 dot-com bubble"
said: Every one of those was followed by a big fall. The CAPE hit its all-time record during the dot-com bubble of two thousand.

what: highlight "only to fall 78% from its peak by October 2002"
said: The Nasdaq peaked on March tenth, two thousand. By October two thousand two, it had fallen seventy-eight percent.

what: highlight "all-time high of 38,957.44 on December 29, 1989"
said: Japan shows the slow version. Its stock market peaked at the end of nineteen eighty-nine.

what: highlight "In 1989, of the world's top 50 companies by market capitalization , 32 were Japanese"
said: And Japan was not some small market. In nineteen eighty-nine, thirty-two of the world's fifty biggest companies were Japanese.

what: highlight "In February 2024, Nikkei 225 reached 39,098.68"
said: And Japan was not some small market. In nineteen eighty-nine, thirty-two of the world's fifty biggest companies were Japanese.

what: highlight "the largest one-day drop in the index's history"
said: And crashes can be fast. On one Monday in October nineteen eighty-seven, the Dow fell twenty-two percent in a single day.

what: highlight "before declining 25% to its low for the year in October 2022"
said: Even the autopilot money did not stop a fall in twenty twenty-two. The S and P five hundred dropped about a quarter from its high that year.

what: highlight "It is not intended as an indicator of impending market crashes"
said: So high prices do not tell you when a crash comes. Shiller himself said this number is not meant to predict crashes. It only says future returns may be lower.

what: highlight "automatically shifting investments from stocks to bonds based on time to planned retirement date"
said: There is one more quiet change coming. Many retirement funds slowly move money out of stocks and into bonds as people get closer to retiring.
